answer: Because the prism index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the echo audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the raven identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator burns for 330 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 330 answers need 330 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
